why: Round 4 tested 8 post-processing variants (EMA smoothing, sticky-band, regime-consensus, horizon-blend, bi-monthly rebalance) to seek deployment-robustness improvements. No variant strictly dominates the baseline. The single decisive outcome is a cost-model correction: Rounds 1-3 applied a flat 20 bps/rebalance (assumes 100 % turnover) whereas actual turnover is ~10 %; the true per-rebalance cost is ~1.9 bps. Corrected full-window LS net Sharpe = 1.32 (not 1.03); Q5 IR = 1.11.

variants_verdict.v3_ema60: test-period Sharpe +0.25 and IR +0.29, but full window -0.06 Sharpe; honest trade-off
variants_verdict.v6_sticky_10pct: runner-up — identical headline, 25 % lower turnover, small test Q5 IR gain
variants_verdict.v8_horizon_blend: REJECTED — autocorrelation inflates Sharpe without real return improvement

turnover_finding: alpha_med_ind is already a low-turnover factor (9.7 % per rebalance full window; 5.7 % on Test). Smoothing has diminishing returns because the signal is slow-moving to begin with.
next_round_focus: Stop accruals variants entirely. The mechanism is saturated.
After 3 months of paper trading evidence, build 2-3 factor ensemble.
